uncited: SWAG extends 3D Gaussian Splatting by conditioning Gaussians on learned appearance embeddings and training unsupervised transient Gaussians to ignore occluders, yielding state-of-the-art results on diverse photo scenes [6875-swag.md].

It distinguishes itself from siblings like Wild-GS by explicitly modeling transient elements as separate Gaussian entities rather than relying solely on depth regularization or visibility maps to mitigate their effects [6875-swag.md].
The number of parameters is independent of time.
Polynomial functions model motion and rotation.
The latter two are translated into residual color through an MLP added to the base color.
The MLP is fixed and only the canonical representation is optimized during fine-tuning.
The field originated with methods like D-NeRF, which established the canonical space paradigm for dynamic NeRFs [8660-d-nerf.md].
